 IRS Enhances Tax Pro Account, Empowering Professionals to Make Client Payments Online
 Published: Nov 14, 2026 
 by Sarah Lewis 
 In Small Business News 
 The IRS is stepping up its game for tax professionals, and small business owners should take note. The agency has expanded its Tax Pro Account capabilities, allowing authorized tax professionals to make essential payments on behalf of their business clients online. This new feature could significantly streamline tax management for small businesses, providing a more efficient and less stressful experience during tax season.
 Previously, tax professionals could only view client balances and payment activity through the Tax Pro Account, but with the recent update, they can now make payments for several critical business tax obligations. Authorized personnel can handle full or partial balances, amend returns, file for extensions, contest proposed tax assessments, and make federal tax deposits—all from one secure online service.
 “Expanding online services that enable tax professionals to do more for their clients advances the goal of making the IRS a digital-first agency,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “For taxpayers who rely on tax professionals, this change will save time and make it easier for them to meet their tax obligations.” This shift towards a more digital approach by the IRS aligns with many small business owners’ preference for fast, efficient processes.
 One of the critical advantages of the new capabilities is the time-saving aspect. Business owners often juggle numerous responsibilities, and tax compliance can be a daunting task. With tax professionals now able to make payments quickly and securely online, small businesses can focus more on their operations rather than tax details. For example, if a business is facing a looming tax deadline, knowing that their tax professional can quickly address payments can relieve a significant amount of stress.
 In practical terms, having tax professionals manage payments simplifies the workflow. Tax professionals must have the appropriate authorizations for each task, ensuring that every payment is made correctly and in compliance with IRS standards. This reduces the risk of errors that could lead to penalties or complicated disputes further down the line.
 While the benefits are clear, small business owners should also be aware of potential challenges that come with these changes. First and foremost, the need for strong relationships with trusted tax professionals becomes more critical than ever. As these professionals gain the ability to handle payments directly, business owners must ensure they work with reputable individuals who understand their specific tax situations and have the necessary authorizations in place.
 Moreover, the digital transformation of tax processes does require some adaptation. Business owners may need to familiarize themselves with the functionalities of the Tax Pro Account, including how to grant the necessary authorizations to their tax professionals. This step is crucial to ensure that their tax matters are handled seamlessly.
 It’s also worth noting that while this new capability simplifies processes, it requires business owners to maintain transparency and ongoing communication with their tax professionals. If business owners are not aware of what payments are being made or why, it could lead to misunderstandings or a lack of trust.
 As small businesses navigate this evolving landscape, they should consider regular check-ins with their tax advisors to ensure all aspects of their tax filings and payments are accounted for. Utilizing the features of the expanded Tax Pro Account can make tax-related tasks much easier, but a collaborative effort is essential for a smooth experience.
 The IRS’s push for a digital-first approach reflects a growing trend in tax management, painting a promising picture for small businesses as they seek efficient ways to meet their tax obligations. As tax professionals build greater capabilities through initiatives like the Tax Pro Account, small businesses can expect a more streamlined and supportive environment for handling their tax responsibilities.
 For more information about the Tax Pro Account and its new features, visit the IRS website at Tax Pro Account .
